reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item. They correct the earlier advice, reason from the tracemalloc-versus-working-set gap to native or tmpfs memory, and give a memory.stat, live-image-count, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX and memray diagnostic ladder with confirm or rule-out criteria. B edges ahead with a more actionable stopgap (request-count recycling via --limit-max-requests or gunicorn --max-requests instead of a timer) and a sync resize example that does not block the event loop, whereas A's sample runs blocking Pillow work inside an async def.

A: Example resize function is async def but performs blocking Pillow decode/resize on the event loop (practical flaw rather than strict factual error)
B: Says the container 'grows by gigabytes' while the observed growth is bounded by a 1Gi limit (minor exaggeration)
